summary: **Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member Shri Harish Dudani, Member Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member** Application under Sections 14 and 15 (1) of Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 15 (3) and Regulation 9 (4) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedures, Terms and Conditions for Grant of trading license and other related matters) Regulations, 2020 for down-gradation of inter-State trading licence in electricity from Category ‘I’ to Category ‘V’. **Statkraft Markets Private Limited,** 401, 4[th] Floor, D-1, Salcon Rasvilas Building, Saket District Centre, New Delhi – 110017 ** Petitioner** Shri Tabrez Malawat, Advocate, SMPL Shri Syed Hamza, Advocate, SMPL Shri Sourajit Sarkar, Advocate, SMPL The Petitioner, Statkraft Markets Private Limited (formerly known as SN Power Markets Private Limited), has filed the present petition seeking down-gradation of its inter-State trading licence in electricity from Category ‘I’ to Category ‘V’. 2. Vide order dated 21.6.2012 in Petition No. 115/TDL/2012, SN Power Markets Private Limited (Now, Statkraft Markets Private Limited) was granted a Category-I licence for inter-State trading in electricity in whole of India in accordance with the provisions of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Order in Petition No. 13/TD/2026 Page 1 Conditions for grant of trading license and other related matter) Regulations, 2009 (‘Trading Licence Regulations, 2009’), subject to the terms and conditions contained in the said licence. Subsequently, based on the request of the trading licensee, the Commission vide order dated 17.11.2014 changed the name of the Petitioner company from ‘SN Power Markets Private Limited’ to ‘Statkraft Markets Private Limited’ pursuant to the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of Companies, Delhi, on 23.8.2014. 3. The Petitioner has submitted that it has regularly paid the annual licence fee for the Category ‘I’ licence for the respective financial years from 2012–2013 to 2025– 2026. The Petitioner has submitted that, on account of adverse market conditions, severe competition, the lack of expected growth in the power market, and the assessment of future business potential in power trading, Statkraft Markets Private Limited is seeking down-gradation of its trading licence from Category ‘I’ to Category ‘V’. The Petitioner has submitted that it intends to engage in trading activities not more than 500 MUs annually. 4. The Petitioner has submitted that its trading volumes have steadily declined over recent financial years, further justifying the downgrade to ensure compliance with the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020, and the terms of the trading licence. 5. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner company has complied with all requirement for downgradation of trading licence and requested to reserved the order in the matter. Order in Petition No. 13/TD/2026 Page 2 _“(4) The Trading Licensee shall make an appropriate application accompanied by prescribed fees for up-gradation of its licence to a higher category or down-gradation of its licence to a lower category in order to fulfil the conditions of these regulations in accordance with the procedure specified in Regulation 15 of these regulations.”._ _(a) The Trading Licensee may file an application to the Commission for down gradation of its licence to a lower category at any time:_ _Provided that the Trading Licensee shall not be allowed to apply for upgradation within the same Year._ _(b) The Trading Licensee shall be required to upload the audited special balance sheet to support the compliance of New Worth requirement for lower category licence._ 8. The Petitioner has filed the present application for the down-gradation of its licence in accordance with the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020. On perusal of the application, we observe that the Petitioner, being an existing trading licensee, fulfils all technical requirements for the grant of a Category ‘V’ inter-State trading licence specified in Regulation 3(2) of the Trading Licence Regulations 2020. As regards the net worth requirements for Category ‘V’, Regulation 3 (3) (a) of the Trading Licence Regulations, 2020 provides that a person applying for a Category ‘V’ trading licence should have a net worth of Rs. 2 crore and should have maintained minimum current ratio and liquidity ratio of 1:1 on the date of Audited Special Balance Sheet accompanying the Petition. Order in Petition No. 13/TD/2026 Page 3 Order in Petition No. 13/TD/2026 Page 4 Order in Petition No. 13/TD/2026 Page 5 11. Based on the above, the net worth, current ratio and liquidity ratio of the Petitioner are as under: 13. Let an extract copy of this order be sent to the Central Government (Ministry of Power) and the Central Electricity Authority in terms of sub-section (7) of Section 15 of the Electricity Act, 2003, for their information and record. 14. We direct that the necessary endorsement be made on the licence issued to the Petitioner with regard to the change of Category of the licensee. Order in Petition No. 13/TD/2026 Page 6 CERC Website S.
